raw_plan.interpretation: I interpreted this as one acquisition email for a solution-aware technical founder who personally manages a website. The email should earn an initial evaluation, not assume the recipient currently uses GA4 or ask them to switch analytics. The primary next step is the documented live demo.

intent.desired_action: View Fathom's live demo and decide whether its single-page dashboard merits a trial.

raw_plan.reader: A technical founder who personally manages a website and wants a direct view of traffic without analytics administration becoming another project.
raw_plan.reader_segment: A technical founder who built the site himself and gave up on GA4 somewhere around the third Explore report
raw_plan.reader_scope: Write at audience level. Do not assume a particular recipient currently uses GA4, has a cookie banner, has attempted a migration, or uses any named framework. Recipient fit should be verified before outreach.
raw_plan.promise: A founder can inspect Fathom's single-page analytics dashboard before installing anything and decide whether it provides the direct traffic view they want.
raw_plan.orientation: Fathom is a paid hosted website analytics service for founders who want pageviews and traffic sources presented on one dashboard page without analytics cookies.
raw_plan.arc: In this single-email campaign, move the reader from abstract comparison of analytics products to a concrete, no-install inspection of the dashboard they would actually use.
raw_plan.sequence_rationale: The reader is already solution-aware, so the email should not explain why website analytics matter or presume a current GA4 complaint. A live demo is the lowest-friction documented action and directly exposes the primary proposition: the dashboard is one page. Installation, privacy, migration, integrations, testimonials, and pricing would create additional arguments, so they stay out of the primary email. The alternative proposition is a separate side-by-side trial argument if the demo-led approach underperforms.

emails.selection_reason: The selected reader wants a quick traffic read, and the current dossier directly links that need to Fathom's documented single-page dashboard. The live demo lets a cold reader judge that interface before accepting installation or trial friction.
emails.target_audience: A technical founder who personally owns the site stack and is evaluating simpler website analytics.
emails.job: Get the reader to inspect the live dashboard and decide whether its one-page presentation is worth testing on their own site.
emails.single_idea: You do not have to replace or install analytics to find out whether Fathom's one-page dashboard gives you the traffic view you want; inspect the live demo first.
emails.felt_need: I want the basic traffic answer in one look instead of hunting through report screens.
emails.mechanism: Fathom presents its analytics in a single-page dashboard. The live demo lets the reader inspect that dashboard directly; in the product, the dashboard is live and real-time.

alternative_arguments.selection_reason: This is a viable second commercial bet for a technical founder who wants to evaluate the product in their own environment without immediately removing any existing analytics. It uses the documented installation and side-by-side trial mechanics instead of the primary demo argument.
alternative_arguments.single_idea: A founder can test Fathom on their own site for seven days while leaving any existing analytics in place.
alternative_arguments.felt_need: I want to evaluate analytics on my own site without turning the test into a full migration.
alternative_arguments.mechanism: Fathom is added with one line of code and can run alongside existing analytics during the seven-day trial. A card is required, but it is not charged until the trial ends, and Fathom emails before billing starts.
alternative_arguments.belief_shift: Before: trying Fathom means committing to a cutover. After: it can be evaluated on the reader's own site alongside any existing analytics before deciding whether to keep it.
must_not_say: Do not claim a complete migration takes one line or any particular amount of time.
Do not assume the recipient currently has another analytics product installed.
Do not imply that the trial is card-free or that cancellation is automatic.
Do not promise identical numbers between Fathom and another analytics product.
Do not claim that a seven-day test establishes long-term suitability.
alternative_arguments.objection: I do not want to remove an existing analytics setup merely to evaluate another product.
alternative_arguments.next_step_decision: Decide whether Fathom's output on the reader's own site is useful enough to keep after the trial.
alternative_arguments.next_step_value: The trial lets the reader add Fathom to a site and run it alongside any existing analytics for seven days before billing begins.
alternative_arguments.next_step_limit: The trial requires a card and installation of the script. It does not establish migration effort, numerical parity with another tool, or long-term fit.
alternative_arguments.subject_strategy: Present a reversible side-by-side test, without implying that the reader has already decided to migrate.

emails.belief_shift: Before: judging whether Fathom is simpler requires installing it or accepting a sales claim. After: the reader can inspect the actual one-page dashboard first and decide whether a trial is warranted.
must_not_say: Do not say that every recipient currently uses GA4, is frustrated with it, or has attempted to leave it.
Do not claim the historical complaint about GA4 click depth is established as current.
Do not promise that one dashboard page answers every analytics question or eliminates all administration.
Do not state or imply a measured setup time, migration time, or time saving.
Do not claim Fathom is uniquely simple or that competitors cannot provide a similar dashboard.
Do not claim that avoiding cookies removes every consent or privacy obligation in every jurisdiction.

Do not claim that the dissenting technical concern about identification through IP addresses and user-agent data has been resolved; the supplied evidence does not establish the full anonymisation mechanism or an independent legal determination.
Do not introduce EU isolation, firewall controls, GA4 imports, integrations, email reports, traffic-spike policy, testimonials, or the full pricing structure; they are separate arguments.
Do not claim that viewing the demo proves compatibility with the reader's site or validates production data.
emails.tone: Direct, practical, and lightly cheeky; confident without turning the reader's presumed frustration into a caricature.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether Fathom's single-page dashboard is clear and relevant enough to justify testing it on the reader's own site.
emails.next_step_value: The destination lets the reader click through a live dashboard and inspect the single-page presentation before installing Fathom.
emails.next_step_limit: The demo shows the dashboard experience; it does not verify compatibility, implementation effort, jurisdiction-specific legal duties, or results using the reader's own traffic.
emails.subject_strategy: Earn the open with the low-friction evaluation: see the whole analytics dashboard before changing the site. Avoid generic simplicity claims and presumed GA4 frustration.

events.subject: See the dashboard first
events.preview_text: Inspect Fathom’s single-page, real-time view before changing your site.
events.body:
You can inspect Fathom Analytics’ live dashboard before changing anything on your site. It lets you judge the whole one-page view on its own terms.

Fathom Analytics is website analytics software that puts live visitors, pageviews, top pages, referrers, countries, devices, browsers, events, and UTM campaigns on a single dashboard page. Once its script is installed, the dashboard updates in real time.

If a basic traffic answer currently sends you through layers of reports, this is the useful test: can one page show the information you actually want to check?

The live demo lets you click through that presentation before installing Fathom or deciding to test it with your own traffic. You can inspect the interface first and make that call.

events.message: Email 1, draft 1: "Test analytics without a cutover"
events.subject: Test analytics without a cutover
events.preview_text: Add one line of code and compare Fathom on your own site for seven days.
events.body:
Fathom is added to your site with a single line of code. If you already use another analytics setup, it can keep running alongside Fathom during the trial.

Fathom is website analytics software that puts your site’s traffic into one dashboard. The side-by-side setup lets you inspect its output on your own site before deciding whether it earns a permanent place there.

The trial runs for seven days. A card is required, but it is not charged until the trial ends, and we’ll email you before billing starts.

After that, the subscription renews automatically unless you cancel in your account settings. No ceremonial analytics cutover required.
